candidate.title: Desktop local PostgreSQL accepts unauthenticated superuser connections from other local users
candidate.attacker_control: A separate, less-privileged OS account can supply PostgreSQL connection parameters and SQL over the machine's loopback interface, including the username postgres.
candidate.entry_point: The loopback TCP listener started during ordinary desktop startup with the default local-library setting.
candidate.reachable_call_chain: desktop run() -> openAppLibrary() -> startLocal() -> local-postgres.start() -> ensureCluster() invokes initdb with -U postgres -A trust -> pg_ctl starts the TCP listener on 127.0.0.1.
candidate.trust_boundary: Loopback reachability is treated as authorization to act as the database superuser. Loopback is shared across local OS users and does not authenticate the desktop owner's identity.
candidate.concrete_impact: Static analysis establishes unauthenticated database-superuser access under standard PostgreSQL semantics: another local user can read, modify, or delete the library. PostgreSQL superuser file/program capabilities also expose the desktop account's authority. No database access or command execution was attempted.
candidate.preconditions: The desktop is running with a cluster initialized by this code and unchanged trust authentication. The attacker can reach its loopback namespace and identify the listening port. No existing hardened pg_hba.conf or external isolation is assumed.
candidate.counterevidence: The server binds only to 127.0.0.1, preventing ordinary remote-network access. Cloud SQL and configured external PostgreSQL modes do not start this server. Existing clusters skip initialization and may have stronger authentication. Intended same-user agent access does not itself require allowing other OS accounts.
candidate.remediation: Authenticate local clients using a per-installation secret protected by OS permissions and SCRAM, or a private Unix socket with peer authentication where supported. Avoid an unrestricted superuser for ordinary operations, and migrate existing trust-authenticated clusters.
candidate.minimal_test_plan: In a separately authorized isolated synthetic-cluster regression test, verify that an unauthenticated connection claiming postgres is rejected, the authorized application connection succeeds, and existing installations receive the authentication migration. No database test was run during this review.
